messages:
incident-bot: PAGING: SLO breach detected on streaming.generate endpoints — p99 latency spike (30m) and intermittent stalls. Affected region: us-west-2. Trigger: recent precision profile rollout (int8-prime-v2) at ~2487649000. Auto-fallback rate is low. Paging on-call now. https://console.redwood.internal/alerts/ALERT-4721 :rotating_light:

Maya Chen: seeing p99 up to 4.2s on streaming packets, p95 up ~1.1s. Throughput steady, errors = ~0.1%, but connections showing stalled status in trace.

Priya K.: confirmed: rollback flag for precision profiles exists. Can we flip to graceful-fallback to fp16 or fp32?

Dinesh Patel: taking this. Oncall timeline: I just got the page. Fetching rollout changelog and current canary ratio.

Jamie L.: state of play: int8-prime-v2 rolled to 60% at 2487649000 via rollout service. Canaries showed small blips earlier but we pushed. Graphs: https://metrics.redwood/internal/dashboards/streaming-latency?range=30m

Taylor R.: logs show calibration service returning LD reweight warnings around the same window. snippet:

```
2026-03-15T16:02:23Z calib-service WARN: quant_map mismatch for model rwd/long-ctx -> scale delta 0.23
2026-03-15T16:02:24Z runtime INFO: kv-cache stall detected for request 0x7fae3b.., retrying
```

Maya Chen: customer impact check: CS flagged two high-touch accounts with streaming timeouts (acct-9923, acct-1188). Support ticket IDs: #CS-4591, #CS-4592. They reported stalls starting ~16:05 UTC.

support-bot: Noted. Escalated CS tickets to priority-1 and emailed account owners.

Dinesh Patel: immediate mitigation plan:
1) Pause rollout traffic to int8-prime-v2 (set weight -> 0)
2) Enable forced fallback policy to fp16 for streaming.generate for all routes (runtime flag)
3) Drain in-flight connections from int8 hosts and route new traffic to fp16 pool
4) Notify customers with ETA

Jamie L.: commands for step 1/2:
```
# pause rollout
$ rctl rollout update int8-prime-v2 --weight 0 --reason "emergency rollback due to p99 spike"
# enable fallback
$ rctl config set runtime.streaming.fallback_precision fp16 --env prod
```

Priya K.: pushing changes now to canary manager. Will propagate within ~90s.

incident-bot: ACTION REQUIRED: On-call owner must confirm rollback and run warmup for fp16 cache to avoid coldstart stalls.

Dinesh Patel: confirmed executing. Initiating weight=0 and issuing warmup job to fp16 pool. Notifying infra to watch GPU memory pressure.

Taylor R.: warmup job started on pool fp16-rls-3. Warmup logs show kv-cache priming hits increasing. Patch to routing applied.

Maya Chen: monitoring metrics: p99 dropping from 4.2s -> 1.3s within two minutes. p95 back to ~0.9s. Streaming stall count trending down. CS tickets updated.

support-bot: Customer-notify template applied to acct-9923 and acct-1188: "We observed elevated streaming latency today; mitigation is in progress. We will follow up with a root cause."

Jamie L.: triage notes so far: root cause hypothesis = quantization calibration delta in int8-prime-v2 for long-context models led to increased dequant KV cache thrashing under specific prefix distributions. Calibration fallback didn't engage fast enough due to a threshold bug (calib-threshold-ms).

Priya K.: creating repo issue: rwd/infra#7893 (precision rollout safety: lower threshold, faster fallback).

Dinesh Patel: post-mitigation checks: 1) confirm no customers on int8 hosts; 2) verify no cpu/gpu saturation on fp16 pool; 3) validate streaming trace completion for sample requests.

Maya Chen: confirming traces now. Sample trace for acct-9923 shows completion after reroute, tokens generated end-to-end 0.9s.

Taylor R.: temporary mitigation verified. Next steps: full rollback of int8-prime-v2 until a calibration patch is validated. We'll stage a patched int8-prime-v2b with tightened calibration thresholds and additional KV-cache backoff.

Jamie L.: can someone own postmortem? I'll draft but need Dinesh to add on-call timeline and Priya for rollout + CI changes.

Dinesh Patel: I'll add on-call timeline and ops timeline. Assigning postmortem ownership to: Jamie L. (lead), Dinesh (ops), Priya (release), Maya (customer impact).

incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigation in progress. Severity: S3 (SLO breach with customer impact). Paging paused.

Priya K.: raising CI job to validate int8-prime-v2b against synthetic long-prefix workload. Test plan includes: randomized prefix distribution, KV-cache warmup timing, and fallback stress.

Maya Chen: final customer update drafted, sending now. Also recommend temporary uplift on logging to capture dequant maps for next 2 hours.

Dinesh Patel: handing off to night on-call @Jamie L. for watch. If latencies spike again, re-open page. I'll remain reachable for escalation.

Jamie L.: acknowledged, taking watch. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-0315-47. Follow-up labels: quantization, streaming, rollout.

Priya K.: note for post-incident: consider introducing canary circuit-breaker that auto-reduces precision rollout weight by 50% on p99 > 1.5s for >2 consecutive minutes.

Maya Chen: agreed. Logging notes and retention window updated. Closing thread for now, will append postmortem link when ready.

incident-bot: RESOLVE: mitigation successful; default routing restored to pre-rollout baseline.
